market_question: Will Dan Cox win the 2026 Maryland Governor Republican primary election?
reasoning: Dan Cox won the 2022 Republican primary narrowly (52.4%) with Trump’s endorsement but is a deeply polarizing figure who lost the general election by 30 points. Kelly Schulz, the moderate Hogan‑endorsed runner‑up with 43.6%, could consolidate the anti‑Cox vote more effectively in 2026, especially if Maryland Republicans seek a candidate who can compete against incumbent Wes Moore. Given these dynamics, I estimate Cox’s true probability of winning the 2026 primary is materially lower than the market’s 57.5%.
evidence_points: In the 2022 primary, Cox received 52.4% of the vote while Kelly Schulz took 43.6%, with multiple candidates splitting the non‑Cox vote.

Cox’s extreme profile (Trump ‘Stop the Steal’ activist, organizer of Jan. 6 bus trips, censured by House GOP) makes him a weak general‑election candidate, which could push primary voters toward a more electable moderate.
The Maryland governorship will be open in 2026 (Larry Hogan term‑limited) and the GOP hasn’t held it since 2023, increasing pressure to nominate a candidate who can win in a blue‑leaning state.
Trump’s endorsement helped Cox in 2022, but the 2026 primary will occur after the 2024 presidential election — if Trump loses again, his influence in a state like Maryland may be diminished.
